words.gloss: Samavartin, 'acting evenly', an epithet of Yama (standard)

hindi: ये सभी समवर्ती यानी यम के वश में गए हुए जानने चाहिए।
english: All these are to be known as gone under the sway of Samavartin (Yama).
notes: 'ete' refers to signs listed before this unit. Samavartin (literally 'acting evenly') is a standard epithet of Yama (standard); read as genitive singular, 'of Samavartin'. 'sarva eva ete' is printed as one string: sarve eva ete, with the usual e-before-vowel sandhi.

hindi: जिसकी गर्दन, ललाट और हृदय ठंडे होकर पसीजते हैं
english: He whose neck, forehead and heart sweat while cold
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in the next unit ('uṣṇo'paraḥ pradeśaś ca ... tasya'). 'śītalam' is neuter singular, agreeing with the neuter dvandva compound. Whether the sweat or the parts are cold is not decided by the Sanskrit.

hindi: और दूसरा प्रदेश यानी भाग गरम है; उसकी शरण देवता हैं।
english: And the other region is hot; his refuge is the deities.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue the relative clause of the previous unit ('yasya'). Copula understood in 'uṣṇaḥ aparaḥ pradeśaḥ' and in 'śaraṇaṃ tasya devatāḥ'. 'The other region' is not specified in the text.

hindi: जो सूक्ष्म ज्योति वाला, अनेकाग्र यानी जो एकाग्र यानी एक बिन्दु पर टिका हुआ नहीं है, दुश्छाय यानी बुरी कान्ति वाला और सदा दुर्मना यानी खिन्न मन वाला है।
english: He who is of small light (aṇujyotis), not one-pointed in mind (anekāgra), ill-lustred or ill-complexioned (duśchāya), and always low-spirited.
notes: 'jyotis' (light) is not specified: eye-light or bodily lustre are both possible. 'anekāgra' is read as an-ekāgra (not one-pointed); aneka-agra (many-pointed) gives the same sense. 'chāyā' can mean lustre, complexion or shadow. The sentence has no main verb here; the relative clause continues in the next unit (appears to).

words.gloss: offering; eaters: bali-eaters (balibhuj, probably crows; probable)

hindi: जिसकी रखी हुई बलि को बलिभुज यानी सम्भवतः कौए नहीं खाते।
english: He whose set-out offering (bali) the bali-eaters (balibhuj, probably crows) do not eat.
notes: 'balibhuj' literally means 'eater of the bali offering'; the usual dictionary sense is crow (probable); other bali-eating beings are not excluded by the word. 'praṇīta' here taken as 'set out, offered' agreeing with 'balim'. The relative clause 'yasya ...' has its main clause outside this unit.

hindi: और जो बिना कारण मेधा यानी बुद्धि, शोभा, उपचय यानी वृद्धि और श्री यानी समृद्धि
english: And he who, without cause, intellect (medhā), beauty (śobhā), growth (upacaya), prosperity (śrī)
notes: GROUPING: the verb 'prāpnoti' is in the next unit; the four objects here depend on it. Translation ends where the unit ends.
lines_deva: निर्निमित्तं च यो मेधां शोभामुपचयं श्रियं
lines_iast: nirnimittaṃ ca yo medhāṃ śobhāmupacayaṃ śriyaṃ

hindi: पाता है, अथवा इनसे पतन यानी ह्रास पाता है, वह यम के घर को पहुँचता है।
english: obtains, or from these a falling away (vibhraṃśa); he reaches the abode of Yama.
notes: GROUPING: completes the sentence begun in the previous unit (appears to). 'ato vā' is ambiguous (from these, or 'from this cause'); read as 'or, from these, a falling away': the sense is a sudden gain or a sudden loss without cause. 'kṣaya' is masculine 'abode'.

hindi: जिस स्वस्थ या रोगी की गुण और दोष से बनी
english: Whose (one) made up of guṇa (quality) and doṣa, of a healthy or of an ill person
notes: GROUPING: the noun 'prakṛtiḥ' (agreeing with 'mayī') and its verb are in the next unit. 'guṇa' is kept as the doctrinal term; it is not specified further here. Elliptical: translation ends with the unit.

hindi: प्रकृति यानी स्वाभाविक अवस्था बदल जाती है; अनुमानित पाठ पर, वह छह मास तक जीवित नहीं रहता।
english: The natural state (prakṛti) goes into change; on a conjectural reading, he does not live six months.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ṣaṇmāsānta' is not a grammatical form (antaḥ/antam/ante); 'ṣaṇmāsān na sa jīvati' ('he does not live six months') gives a regular form and fits the signs that follow; syllable count is the same (16) either way

notes: Emendation is conjectural. As printed, 'ṣaṇmāsānta sa jīvati' would read 'he lives to the end of six months' (another possible repair is 'ṣaṇmāsānte'); the two sense-options differ (he lives up to six months, or not even six). GROUPING: continues 43 (subject 'prakṛtiḥ' with 'yasya ... guṇadoṣamayī'); the sentence is 'whose prakṛti ... changes, he ...'. Reviewer: ta/na is a known OCR confusion in this print, so 'ṣaṇmāsānta sa' may be 'ṣaṇmāsānna sa' (one letter); this favours 'ṣaṇmāsān na' but is not proof. OPEN for owner: 'does not live six months' vs 'lives to the end of six months' (opposite senses).

hindi: भक्ति, शील, स्मृति, त्याग, बुद्धि और बल, बिना कारण
english: Devotion (bhakti), character (śīla), memory (smṛti), giving up (tyāga), intellect (buddhi) and strength (bala), without cause.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue in the next unit; 'ahetukam' (without cause) probably belongs with the verb 'nivartante' there. The object of 'bhakti' is not stated. 'tyāga' may be read 'generosity' as well as 'giving up'.

hindi: ये छह, छह मास में मरने वाले से हट जाते हैं।
english: These six turn away from one who will die in six months.
notes: Completes 45 (appears to): the six are bhakti, śīla, smṛti, tyāga, buddhi, bala. 'ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ' is an instrumental of time, 'in six months'.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: मतवाले के समान चाल, वाणी, कम्पन और मोह, एक मास में मरने वाले के।
english: On a conjectural reading: gait, speech, trembling and bewilderment like those of a drunk man, in one who will die in a month.

text_flags.why: possible: 'gāti' is not a standard word for 'gait'; 'gati' (going, gait) fits the drunk comparison; the sense is unaffected

notes: 'māsān' is māsāt (ablative of time) before m. Whether 'mattavat' qualifies only gait and speech or all four items is not decided. Elliptical: no verb. Reviewer: 'gātra' (limb/body) for printed 'gāti' is an equally short repair (gātra-vāk-kampa-mohāḥ); not decidable from the print.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: नष्ट होता है; शब्द अज्ञाननूषड्हात् अस्पष्ट है; केश नोचने की पीड़ा।
english: On a conjectural reading: is lost; the word 'ajñānanūṣaḍhāt' is unclear; the pain of hair-plucking.

text_flags.why: damaged print: the whole line is printed as one token with no spaces; 'ajñānanūṣaḍhāt' cannot be restored (one guess only: 'ṣaḍahāt' 'in six days'; 'ajñāna' and 'nū' unexplained); 'vedanām' (accusative) has no verb that takes it, so 'naśyati' may also be wrong

notes: Damaged. Only 'keśa-luñcana-vedanā' (pain of hair-plucking) is firm. The grammatical frame is unknown, so no verb-object relation is claimed between 'naśyati' and 'vedanām'.

hindi: और जिसका आहार गले तक नहीं जाता, गले के रोग के सिवा
english: And he whose food does not go to the throat (kaṇṭha), except for a throat ailment.
notes: 'ṛte' takes the ablative. The sentence continues with a result beyond this unit (appears to); the translation ends with the unit.
lines_deva: न याति यस्य चाहारः कंठं कंठामयादृते
lines_iast: na yāti yasya cāhāraḥ kaṃṭhaṃ kaṃṭhāmayādṛte

hindi: सेवक विपरीत चलते हैं और प्रेत की आकृति उत्पन्न होती है।
english: Servants go contrarily, and the form of a preta (departed spirit, ghost) arises.
notes: 'udīryate' is taken as middle 'arises'; the passive 'is uttered/stirred up' is also possible. 'pretākṛti' is read 'the form of a preta'; whose form (the person's) is not stated.

hindi: जिसकी नींद निरन्तर हो अथवा बिलकुल न हो, वह जीवित नहीं रहता।
english: He whose sleep is constant, or not at all, does not live.
notes: 'naiva vā' is read 'or not at all', so the sleep is either constant or absent.
lines_deva: यस्य निद्राभवेन्नित्या नैव वा न स जीवति
lines_iast: yasya nidrābhavennityā naiva vā na sa jīvati

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: मुख आँसुओं से भर जाता है और दोनों पैर बहुत पसीजते हैं।
english: On a conjectural reading: the face is filled with tears, and both feet sweat greatly.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vakram' (crooked) gives no sense, 'vaktram' (face) is expected; the half-line has 15 syllables as printed and 16 with 'āpūryate', which also fits the genitive 'aśrūṇām'

notes: Printed 'ārpyate' (ā-√ṛ caus. pass.) would mean 'is placed / delivered', not 'is filled'; `words` therefore carry the conjectured 'āpūryate' ('is filled'), as in the text_flag. Both 'ārpyate' and 'āpūryate' sit oddly with the genitive 'aśrūṇām' (instrumental expected); the whole repair is conjectural. 'svidyataḥ' is 3rd dual, agreeing with 'caraṇau'. 'vaktra' can be face or mouth.

hindi: और जो यम के राज्य को जाने वाला है उसकी आँख व्याकुलता में पड़ जाती है।
english: And the eye of one who will go to the realm of Yama falls into agitation (ākulatā).
notes: 'cakṣuścākulatāṃ' is cakṣuḥ ca ākulatām (ś before c; ca + ā). 'ākulatā' = agitation, confusion, disorder.

hindi: जिन भावों में वह पहले रमता है, उनसे अरति वाला वह जीवित नहीं रहता।
english: Displeased (arati) with those things (bhāva) in which he formerly delighted, he does not live.
notes: 'aratiḥ' is feminine 'displeasure', used as a predicate or adjective of the unstated subject. 'bhāva' = state, thing, object of enjoyment.

hindi: और वैद्य पूछे जाने पर भी सुनने में कठिन मृत्यु को कहे।
english: And the physician, even when asked, should tell the death that is hard to hear.

text_flags.why: possible: two 'ca' in a row is odd; न्न could be misread as च्च in the scan, which would give 'should not tell, even if asked'; NOT adopted here, the printed reading is translated

notes: The doubled 'ca' is left partly untranslated (the second 'ca' has no clear function). If the intended reading is 'kathayen na ca' the meaning would be the opposite ('should not tell'). GROUPING: 'maraṇam' appears to be completed by the genitives in the next unit. 'kathayet' is 10th-class, not causative.

words.gloss: gone; breath: one whose life-breath is gone

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं उसके, बन्धुओं और मित्रों के; और उसकी चिकित्सा करने की इच्छा नहीं करनी चाहिए।
english: On a conjectural reading: of one whose life-breath has gone (gatāsu), of kinsmen and friends; and one should not wish to treat him.

text_flags.why: possible: 'icchet taṃ cikitsitam' does not parse naturally; the infinitive 'cikitsitum' ('to treat') is expected after 'icchet'; a final -um misprinted -aṃ is plausible

notes: 'na cecchet' = na ca icchet (ca + i = e). 'gatāsu' (literally 'whose breath has gone') is used of one who is dying or dead; treatment being discussed, a dying person is probably meant. The genitives 'gatāsoḥ' and 'bandhumitrāṇām' may belong to 'maraṇam' (death) of the previous unit; their exact relation is not certain. The unit as a whole is elliptical.

words.gloss: Yama; messenger; piśāca (a class of demon); beginning with

hindi: क्योंकि परासु यानी जिसके प्राण चले गए हैं वह यम के दूतों, पिशाचों आदि द्वारा उपासित होता है यानी उसके निकट रहा जाता है,
english: since one whose life-breath has departed (parāsu) is attended by those beginning with Yama's messengers and piśācas,

text_flags.why: possible: long ū in '-rūpāsyate' is a print slip for 'parāsur upāsyate'

notes: 'yat' is the conjunction 'since' (gender does not agree with parāsuḥ, m.). 'ādya' = 'beginning with', no 'such as' is supplied. GROUPING: continues in the next unit (appears to).

hindi: औषधों के वीर्य यानी शक्ति को नष्ट करने वालों द्वारा; इसलिए उससे बचना चाहिए।
english: by those who destroy the potencies (vīrya) of medicines; therefore one should avoid him.
notes: Continues 57 (appears to): 'ghnadbhiḥ' qualifies the instrumentals of 57. Agent of 'parivarjayet' is not stated ('one').

hindi: रिष्ट यानी मृत्यु के लक्षण के बिना मृत्यु नहीं है, और जिसमें रिष्ट देखा गया है ऐसा जीवन भी है।
english: There is no death without riṣṭa (sign of death), and there is life in which riṣṭa has been seen.
notes: 'ariṣṭam' is read a-riṣṭa 'without riṣṭa', agreeing with 'maraṇam'; 'dṛṣṭariṣṭam' = dṛṣṭa-riṣṭa (not dṛṣṭa-ariṣṭa, which would show ā). Copula understood in the second clause. Reviewer: ca may carry nāsti into the second clause: 'there is no death without riṣṭa, and no life (in one) in whom riṣṭa has been seen'. This fits u62 (death in riṣṭa is certain) and u60 better than the translation given; OPEN for owner.
lines_deva: अरिष्टं नास्ति मरणं दृष्टरिष्टं च जीवितं
lines_iast: ariṣṭaṃ nāsti maraṇaṃ dṛṣṭariṣṭaṃ ca jīvitaṃ

hindi: जहाँ रिष्ट नहीं है वहाँ रिष्ट का ज्ञान; और रिष्टों में नहीं, निपुणता के अभाव से।
english: In the absence of riṣṭa, knowledge of riṣṭa; and not in riṣṭas, from lack of skill.
notes: Elliptical (no verb). Probably it means a false recognition of riṣṭa where none exists and a failure to recognise real riṣṭas, both from lack of skill; this is an inference, the Sanskrit does not say 'false' or 'failure'.

hindi: यह चरक का वचन है; सुश्रुत के द्वारा तो पढ़ा जाता है।
english: This is the statement of Caraka; but by Suśruta it is recited.
notes: 'iti' is read as 'thus, this'. The object of 'paṭhyate' is not stated (the statement of the following unit appears to be meant). Caraka and Suśruta are taken as names of the two authorities.

hindi: क्योंकि रिष्ट होने पर मृत्यु निश्चित है; वह, कहते हैं, निर्मल ब्राह्मणों द्वारा
english: For death in riṣṭa is certain; that, it is said, by stainless brāhmaṇas
notes: GROUPING: the verb 'nivāryate' is in the next unit, with the instrumentals continuing there. 'tat' (that) is the neuter subject of the next verb; its referent (death or its certainty) is not stated here. 'dhruvam' could also be adverbial ('surely').

words.gloss: rasāyana (rejuvenation therapy; standard); austerity; giving; intent on

hindi: और रसायन यानी पुनर्यौवनकारी चिकित्सा, तप और दान में लगे हुओं द्वारा हटाया जाता है।
english: and is warded off by those intent on rasāyana (rejuvenation therapy), austerity (tapas) and giving (dāna).
notes: Completes 62 (appears to): 'tat' of 62 is the subject. 'rasāyana' = rejuvenation therapy (standard).

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर नाम के लिए: कृष्णात्रेय, रिष्ट दो प्रकार का, स्थिर और अस्थिर के भेद से।
english: On a conjectural reading of the name: Kṛṣṇātreya, riṣṭa twofold, by the division into stable and unstable.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kṛṣṇātareya' is not a known name; 'kṛṣṇātreya' (Kṛṣṇa Ātreya) fits, and the half-line has 17 syllables as printed and 16 with the correction

notes: No verb in the Sanskrit (probably 'says/holds' is understood). The 'twofold' division is stable (sthira) and unstable (asthira) riṣṭa, as taken up in the next units.

hindi: दोषों की अधिकता से भी रिष्ट का आभास उत्पन्न हो सकता है।
english: Even from an abundance of the doṣas, a semblance of riṣṭa (riṣṭābhāsa) may arise.
notes: 'api' is taken with 'doṣāṇām' ('even from the doṣas'), meaning a riṣṭa-like appearance arises without real riṣṭa.

hindi: उन दोषों के शान्त होने पर शान्त हो जाए; परन्तु स्थायी निश्चय ही मृत्यु के लिए है।
english: On the subsiding of those doṣas it would subside; but the lasting (one) is certainly for death.
notes: GROUPING: continues 65 (appears to): the unstated subject of 'śāmyet' is the riṣṭābhāsa of 65, and 'sthāyi' stands for the stable riṣṭa of 64. Copula understood in the second clause. 'sthāyi' could be sthāyī (m.) or sthāyi (n.), so no gender is given.

hindi: आयुर्वेद यानी जीवन के शास्त्र का सम्पूर्ण फल, जो आयु के ज्ञाता में प्रतिष्ठित है।
english: The whole fruit of Āyurveda (the science of life), which is established in one who knows lifespan (āyurjña).
notes: 'yat' is a relative pronoun agreeing with 'phalam' (n.). 'āyurjña' = one who knows the span of life; the main clause is carried by the next unit (appears to).

words.gloss: riṣṭa (sign of death); knowledge; attentive to

hindi: इसलिए वैद्य को सदा ही रिष्ट के ज्ञान का आदर करने वाला होना चाहिए।
english: Therefore the physician should always be attentive to the knowledge of riṣṭa.
notes: 'ādṛta' is taken as active 'regardful, attentive'. The alternative 'honoured for knowledge of riṣṭa' is possible but less natural.

words.gloss: abnormal; activity, movement; relating to knowledge

hindi: इस प्रकार विकृतेहाविज्ञानीय नामक दसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus the tenth chapter, named Vikṛtehāvijñānīya.
notes: Colophon; the closing 'iti' is 'thus'. The title is kept transliterated; analysed as vikṛta-īhā-vijñānīya it probably means 'relating to knowledge of abnormal activities', not applied in the translation.
